source_caption:
Much is made of Ursula Andress’s first appearance in 𝐃𝐫. 𝐍𝐨 (𝟏𝟗𝟔𝟐) - but in the novel, Honey Ryder emerges from the sea completely naked. When she spots Bond, she drops her shells so that one hand can cover her crotch, while the other hand hides her broken nose. This would have been impossible to depict in a big studio film at the time, due to the Hays Code censorship rules, which led to the use of Honey’s iconic white bikini. Even when censorship attitudes softened somewhat over the following years, the James Bond series has generally stayed away from depictions of nudity to keep the movies accessible to broad audiences.

Rate 𝐃𝐫. 𝐍𝐨 (𝟏𝟗𝟔𝟐) out of ten. 👀 🔟
